Entries.Text: Pick the two projects of the port: the input project the maps are read from (Dark Souls III) and the output project they are written into (Elden Ring). The input project is never written. Only the output project's folder is.
No {0} project. Create one in Smithbox first.
Reads the stored projects again, for projects created in Smithbox while this window was open.
Ready: open the Map section to port a map.
{0}: the game folder {1} does not exist.
{0}: the project folder {1} does not exist.
The input and output projects use the same folder.
No Oodle library (oo2core) in {0}: Elden Ring's files can't be read without it.
Could not read the project file {0}.
Pick the input and output projects in the Home section first.
Ports a whole map of {0} into an existing map of {1}: every map piece the DS3 map places, with its materials and textures, its collision, and the map's parts at their DS3 positions plus the offset.
Reading the maps of both projects...
Could not read the maps of the picked projects.
Added to every ported part's DS3 position, to place the DS3 map away from the ER map's own content (for example far below it).

Before the port is added, removes the ER map's vanilla map pieces, collisions, connect collisions, assets, enemies and dummies from its MSB, with the events that place them. Player starts and anything your project added stay. The map's files stay on disk, so running again with this off brings them back.
Rebuilds the DS3 map's h and l collision as Elden Ring collision in the ER map's binders, with the collision surfaces remapped, and adds its collision parts.

Ports the DS3 map's static and breakable objects as Elden Ring assets: their models, textures, physics (including the broken state) and an asset param row each, written into the output project's regulation. Animated and cloth objects are left out.
On: breakable objects keep their broken state and break as they do in DS3. Off: they are ported as normal static objects (the intact model and its collision, a static asset param row).
Encloses the ported map in a box that isn't drawn but casts shadows, so the sun and sky don't light it, as Elden Ring's catacombs do. The box covers the ported collision with a 30 m margin.
Writes into {0}. Files the port wrote before are replaced, so it can be run again.
Finished with problems: {0} failed checks, {1} warnings. See the log below.
